utterances.text: Not in principle. However, it says here in agreement with the NGS. I repeat, you don't have the original request. Again, we can't see what the request said and what was added by hand either by the chief or the chief of the logistics sector. I can't remember what the original said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, would you have -- never mind. I'll step back from that. Why do you say this document in principle is not consistent with the procedure that you had described earlier?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Because I would not have been allowed to reply directly to the 608th base. I would have had to follow the route that I explained, unless it had been explicitly requested for me to shorten that route. However, I'm not in a position to prove what happened one way or another because the original request is missing. We don't have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under similar conditions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal, please. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number marked for identification and kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh, that's why I asked under the same conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Under seal, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal but not marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P623 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please bring up 65 ter 8979 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you'll see this is a document from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska dated 19 June 1995. And it says "very urgent." "To the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia ..." and then "... personally to the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ." Do you see that? Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then below that we see a subtitle, if you will, called: "Help and ammunition, a request." And the next paragraph describes what's referred to as a Muslim offensive and the resistance put up by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I haven't had a chance to read it yet, and I haven't read it. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what army did the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps belong to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I am not familiar with the structure of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if we continue down to the request, and now we are on the second page of the English version, there's a paragraph beginning with "However ..." and it says: "However, due to the fact that the Sarajevo-Trnovo road communication is not safe, we are not able to bring in the supplies and to reinforce the units of the SRK and the HK, Herzegovina corps." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then below that, it says: "For the above-mentioned reasons, we need your urgent help with the following quantities of ammunition as follows ..." and then we see below that a list of different kinds of ammunition. Are you seeing that with me?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And then we see at the bottom, towards the bottom -- actually, if we can go to the next page in the B/C/S version, please, and we see that it's from Kommandant Ratko Mladic personally?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question for you right now is, just up to this point, by sending his request to the VJ General Staff, was General Mladic following the established procedure that you described to us earlier today?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so, but I don't know what the procedure agreed was because this is something that is not within my purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you remember the procedure that you described to us in the last session?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you told -- do you recall telling us that a request was supposed to come from the VRS Main Staff to the VJ General Staff? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I recall that. That's what I was informed -- that's how I was informed, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So up to this point, General Mladic is following the procedure that you described; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn back to the first page in both versions, please. And, yes, could we also zoom in a bit on the upper part of the B/C/S version, as well, make that a bit bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, up in the top right-hand corner, there's --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There is a handwritten note, and there's some initials. Do you recognise -- do you know -- do you recognise those initials?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it looks like the initials of General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And that note says: "Give it to Ratko so as to have this resolved." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could now turn to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, before we do that, did you receive similar handwritten notes from General Perisic on requests that were forwarded to you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already mentioned that to that effect, see if anything can be given, check, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just need to point out, Your Honours, that one of the General's microphone is apparently turned off, and it's the microphone that he is speaking directly into, so perhaps we should resolve that. Thank you so much, Mr. Usher. If we go to the next page in both documents, please, and can we zoom in on the bottom of each page, please. Not the top but the lower half of each page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see -- we see what appears to be a telegram. Would you agree with that, General?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's from the cabinet of the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, to the logistics sector Lieutenant-Colonel Milovanovic. Did you know -- lieutenant-colonel general, I should say, Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know this gentleman, Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is deceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page in the English version, please. And if we can make that a little bit bigger. And if we could make in the B/C/S version, the text we see at the bottom a bit bigger, as well, please. If we could make the text at the bottom bigger, please. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see that the text here is in Cyrillic -- well, I will ask you. Is that Cyrillic script that we see here in this telegram?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: The telegram is in the Latin script, but the bottom part, the text at the bottom is in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And here it says that the -- "We forward you the telegram from the General Staff of the VRS and inform that you the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia ordered the following: 'Give it to Ratko so as to have this resolved.'" Are you following?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you receive -- actually, then we see "for the chief," and then a signature over a colonel, Sinisa Borovic. What does that phrase mean, "for the chief"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that at this time he had not been appointed the chief yet; he was just acting chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This document is from June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The word "for" means standing in for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And who would the chief be in this context?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he was just standing in for someone at the time because if an officer is not appointed by an order or a decree, then this is the standard form used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this document being introduced through this witness because from the questions of the Prosecutor, the witness only confirmed the content of the document that was read out to him, and the witness himself said that he didn't know anything about the substance of the document itself, such as, for instance, the questions about the signature, and especially so because this is in no way related to his administration. It's a totally different administration. So from where I'm standing, I don't see that there has been a link established between him and this document, and the fact alone that he recognizes the signature or, rather, the initials of General Perisic's is not sufficient ground for basing or for the link between this witness and the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecution's submission, the fact that the witness recognizes the initials of General Perisic actually creates a very strong relationship between the witness and this document. Second of all, the witness was able to tell us that at least the first part of this document up to the point where we see the signature area for General Mladic was consistent with the procedure that he described to us during the last session; that is, requests for materiel and assistance from the VRS would come from the VRS Main Staff to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, and that is what the witness was able to confirm. The witness has described carefully what the procedure was for these requests and how they are acted upon. And he was able to explain that part of this document was consistent with that request, and he was able to recognise the initials of General Perisic. And he was able to tell us that he received similar handwritten notes on a number of occasions similar to what is up at the top right-hand corner. Therefore, Your Honour, the Prosecution would submit there is a relationship established between this witness and this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Briefly. This is the evidence of this witness on procedure, but this witness has nothing to say about this document. He did describe the procedure, and the procedure was followed, and this we can see through the questions of Mr. Saxon, but the witness did not show that he knows anything about this document itself except that he confirmed in reply to Mr. Saxon's questions what the document was about, but this is not sufficient ground to establish a relationship between the witness and the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By majority, the objection is overruled, Moloto dissenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can this document then be given an exhibit number, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so given a number. May it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P624 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please bring up now on the screen 65 ter 8934, and I'm grateful to Ms. Taseva for all her patience with me today. Your Honours -- actually, Your Honours, this 65 ter exhibit is actually three documents, and I'd like to discuss all three of them with the witness, and if we could look first at the second document in this sequence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, this document is from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It's dated the 7th of October, 1993. It says: "Urgent request for issuance of communications equipment submitted to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia ..." And in the English -- yeah, "... personally to the chief." And you'll see that it is a request for some communications equipment. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And again, it is over --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Although it's pretty illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. And again, it's over the signature line of Lieutenant-Colonel General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can zoom in, please, on the upper right-hand corner of the B/C/S version, please, where there's some handwriting. If you could make that a bit bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see a note.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The handwritten note says -- first says: "Andjelkovic, if you can give it, do so." First of all, do you know who the gentleman Andjelkovic was?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was the then-chief of the communications administration at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So we see the name "Andjelkovic" underlined and then the phrase "... if you can give it, do so ..." underlined. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I can make the out the name Andjelkovic, but I cannot read the rest. It's rather blurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Would you take my word for it if it says "... if you can give it, do so"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I have the right to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll retract that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... I do believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recognise any of the handwriting in those first two lines or the initials there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No. I can read a portion of the text, but not the entire text, nor can I make out the initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. In October of 1993, which -- actually, I'm going to finish reviewing these notes before I go to that question. Hopefully you can read the following notes. Under Lieutenant Andjelkovic, it says: "This was at the chief of the Main Staff" -- excuse me. "This was at the Chief of the General Staff. Write down what his position is on it." And then we see a phrase: "My opinion is: Some of our corps commands" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I really don't want to interfere with your leading, but the witness said to you he can read part of that handwritten note and not all of it. Now, you are reading it to him. Who's in the witness box?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I take your point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, are you able to read any of the handwritten note below the top portion?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Colonel Andjelkovic ..." and it says: "First, this was at the NGAs. You say this was his position too. My view, we have corps commands that have not been fully equipped with some communications equipment ..." and then further on, there's something that I cannot recognise. And then it says under 3: "If you have some of what has been requested ..." and then I cannot read the rest. And then at the end, it says: "To General Milovanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can you -- what was General Milovanovic's position in October 1993?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. For awhile, he was the chief of the logistics sector, and I'm not sure whether he was already in this position at this time. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Can we scroll down, please, further down in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There's some more handwriting. Are you able to read that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Stankovic, Stankovic, please -- I cannot make out the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on the rest of that, please, on the rest of that handwritten text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go down to the equivalent part in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It would be the next page, I believe, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to read that handwriting now, General? Is it any better?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Not the entire text. I can make out a word here and there. I think it says: "I think that" -- "that we can issue ..." or "it can be issued ..." And then I can't read a part. Then it says "cable." And then it says "under number 6." I can't make out the rest. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. This request from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, was the forwarding of this request in the Main Staff of the VRS to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia consistent with the procedure that you described to us earlier today about how these requests began?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it seems to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could now, please, look at document ID 0630-5832, which is another document in this 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you intend to tender that separately from the other two?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I tender this, Your Honour, I believe I will tender them altogether, would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But now you are giving us two reference numbers. When we give it an exhibit number, what do we relay that exhibit number to? Do we relay it to 8934, or do we relate it to 0630583?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will take Your Honour's point. At this point, I will seek to tender the last document that we looked at, if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The one on the screen now or the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could have the Court's indulgence for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I -- I think it would be cleaner if we could -- if we could go back to that last document, which was the request, and I will ask that it be tendered into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go back to that last document that was the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We're still -- we need to go back to the last document, which was 65 ter 0630 -- excuse me. Yeah, there we are. Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not object, but I have another problem, Your Honours. My case manager has told me that this document has two different English translations in e-court, so to avoid confusion, could only this translation that we see on the screen now be admitted into evidence. I don't know why it appears in our records that there are two translations of one and the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is your team able to help us identify the other copy so that we get rid of it from the e-court? Otherwise, we will never know six months down the line which was the English version that was admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only ask that the English translation of the document which has the ERN number 0630-5833-ET-1 not be entered -- not be admitted into evidence. And the one on the screen has the number - just let me put my glasses on - it has the number -- well, it ends with 5833, and that may then be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we have that zoomed in, please, that English version so that we can see that ERN number. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is. So I agree that ET-0630-5833 be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, that document with that ERN number ET-0630-5833-0630-5833 is admitted into evidence together with its B/C/S version. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P625.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could now turn, please, to the document with document ID 0630-5832. That was still part of 65 ter 8934. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you will see that this is a document sent to the General Staff of the -- excuse me, sent from the communications administration, part of the operation affairs sector at the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, and there's a subtitle on the left-hand side: "Position on issuance of requested communications equipment submitted." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's addressed to the cabinet of the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ, and it says that this document is in relation to the request made by the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, highly confidential number 12/9-897 dated the 7th of October, 1993, and it describes a position being taken. And in subparagraph 1, it describes how the issue of implementing secure communications was discussed at a meeting, also attended by a representative of the General Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, but the first request was found unacceptable. Paragraph 2, the communications administration does not have the spare pieces of equipment. Paragraph 3, it asks for more information, et cetera. And paragraph 4 says we should discuss this issue at a later time. Do you see a relationship between this document and the previous document that we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document, and I'm not competent to discuss its contents. I think that this is a response by the chief of the communications administration to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you ever receive requests for materiel originating from the VRS - when I say you, I mean the engineering administration - through the procedure, of course, where you did not have the requested equipment or materiel? Did you ever have those situations?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I have already said that we modified the quantities of certain equipment or materiel. I don't remember recalling any requests for equipment or materiel which we did not have at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So in those situations -- when you said "... we modified the quantities of certain equipment or materiel ..." what do you mean by that? Was that in a document? You say you modified the quantities of certain equipment or materiel.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: We reduced the quantities, as I've already explained, because our own units were insufficiently replenished and supplied.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say you reduced the quantities, would you put that in your response to a request?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. In our response, we reduce the quantities that had been asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Does this recommendation from Andjelkovic accord with the procedure that you described to us earlier today for responding to requests for assistance from the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot comment because in the previous document I didn't understand who had sent the document to whom since the signatures are illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we please go -- I can't recall the last exhibit that was admitted, but can we please go back to that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you'll see that this last document that we looked at, this request now with Exhibit number P625, you see in the upper left-hand corner that it comes from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear to me. This first part that the document -- the first part of the route followed by the document, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's directed to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that's clear too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, can we go back to the last document that we were looking at, please, the response from Andjelkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't you want to go through the signatures? The witness said he doesn't know who signed it and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. We'll stay on this document. If we could -- if we scroll down in the English version, please. Next page, please, in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see although there's no signature on the left side, it says: Commander, Lieutenant-Colonel General Ratko Mladic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So in this document, are you able to see the origin of the document and then who it's sent to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we go to the next document that we've been looking at, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see on this next --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, I'm very sorry to bother our Registry officer. If we could go back for a moment to P625, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Isn't this it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This document has not been admitted yet. That is it on the right-hand side. If we could go to the English version of 625.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you see in the upper left-hand corner of the document in B/C/S, can you read the number of the document, General?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on that number, please, in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12/9-897. That's what I can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we go to the next document that we had started to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you see, General, that in the first sentence of that document, there's a reference to document 12/9-897? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see that this was a response from Andjelkovic to the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So does this response from Andjelkovic accord with the procedures that you described to us earlier today as to what the administration should do after it is forwarded a request?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I see that Colonel Andjelkovic sent a response to the cabinet of the Chief of the General Staff, but in the previous document I didn't see that the Chief of the General Staff sent a copy of the request to Andjelkovic or someone in between. And that's the illegible initials underneath the comment I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you received a request, you forwarded a response to the General Staff, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I first sent the response to the cabinet, if that's who I had received it from, or through the logistics sector if that was the way it had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see anything in this document in this response that is inconsistent with the procedure that you described?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: No, because I don't know who is in between Colonel Andjelkovic and the cabinet of the chief of the General Staff. All I understand is that Colonel Andjelkovic did not receive the document from the Chief of the General Staff but from a third person. Whether it's a sector, I cannot decipher here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would seek to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P626.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please call up 0630-5834, document ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, you will see this is a document from the cabinet of the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. This is numbered 81/107. It's dated the 20th of October, 1993, and it's addressed to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's titled: "A Response to a Request For Issuance of Communications Equipment." And then in the line below that, it refers to confidential number 12/9-897, the first document that we looked at. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it's from the chief of the cabinet, Colonel Zivanovic. And we see the language in paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4 contains information regarding the original request. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And again, it is explaining that the VJ is unable to grant the request completely. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would such a document, such a response from the VJ General Staff to the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, would this also be part of the procedure that you described to us earlier?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot comment on the competencies of the head of the cabinet -- of the chief of the cabinet of the chief of the Main Staff. I don't know what his powers were, and I don't know why he signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know whether the General Staff of the -- no, I will strike that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would submit this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object in principle. Four questions were put to the witness about these documents, actually five, and Mr. Saxon was reading parts of these documents, and when he finally asked the witness in line 10 to answer whether he was familiar with the procedure, the witness answered no, so I don't think we have received any feedback on this document from this witness, and this is the main reason for my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the relationship between this witness and this particular document is that this document refers back to the original request, which the witness was able to comment on as being part of the procedures in place at that time. So in the Prosecution's submission, there is a relationship between this witness and this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness did talk about the procedure. However, when it comes to the procedure between the cabinet of the Chief of the General Staff and the Army Republika Srpska and the procedure that existed between the two is something that the witness didn't know, and this is the only thing that Mr. Saxon wanted to hear from him. Your Honours, I don't see this document colliding with my Defence case, and I believe that there are thousands of ways to introduce this document through other witnesses, but I'm objecting, as I said, in principle because the witness provided answers that really don't have anything to do with the document, and I don't want this practice to be introduced as the way the documents are tendered for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection upheld.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please turn to 65 ter 8894.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you abandoning this completely, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, can it be marked for identification? I apologise, Your Honour. I'm going too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response to that one, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, in principle I'll say that I object. I'm against that as well. Again, for the reasons of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But if it's marked for identification and nobody comes to identify it, then it doesn't come in. Isn't that how marking for identification --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You already pointed that to me yesterday, and I'm actually willing to accept your suggestion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. We'll admit it and mark it for identification, please. Is it under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P627 marked for identification under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I have the Registry's assistance in calling up 65 ter 8894, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: General, do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's addressed to the -- it's from the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, sector for logistics -- or excuse me, that is the stamp in the upper left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do you see -- there's a signature at the bottom of the page. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat. Where is the signature?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we focus on the signature that's on the bottom of the page. Can we zoom in on that signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, in the lower corner?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's the chief of General Staff, General Perisic's signature. That's what I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if we can scroll back up, please. General Perisic refers to an order of the President, and maybe to assist General Mihajlovic, if we could zoom in a bit on the B/C/S text to help him a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says: "Pursuant to an order of the President" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "Pursuant to an order of the President dated the 18th of February, 1994, I issued an instruction for replenishment of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres with materiel supplies." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what were the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, and I don't have complete information, mind you, I believe that those were representatives of the Army Republika Srpska and the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina, and they were dealing in personnel issues, hence the title of the two centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And below that, it says: "Despite constant warnings, certain commanding officers of the VJ disobeyed the order and issued equipment for the needs of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre without authorisation." And then it gives a series of directives below that, warnings about to strictly implement the measures and procedures from his instruction, et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While Mr. Saxon is taking a break, can I just ask a question for clarification. What are special units corps? To whom was this addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In handwriting, it says command of KSJ. This was the special units corps, so this means that this document was sent to all units, and this is a copy of the document that was sent to this particular unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we can assist the witness. If we scroll down, the witness will see a stamp of the recipient, and the witness can't see that in B/C/S version. It's at the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It says the corps command of special units where this document was filed on the 17th of August, 1994. Command of the corps of special units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what are special units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a unit as far as I can remember on the strength of that corps. There was a guards brigade, an armoured brigade, a parachute brigade, and I don't know whether there were any others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So this document was not addressed to the sectors like yours, for instance, or the engineering one or the communications sector; it was addressed to the combatting units. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've not seen any of these documents before. I'm not familiar with them. However, as a soldier I can assume that the document was sent to all the organs of the General Staff including all the sectors and all the units that were directly related to the General Staff, and the corps of special units was directly related to the General Staff as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I don't understand the question, but I don't think I can take the matter any further. You can carry on, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We spoke briefly about the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres. Where were these personnel centres located?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they were located in Belgrade in one of the General Staff's buildings, on the premises of the personnel administration, I believe. I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly where their office was because I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall who was the officer in charge of the 30th Personnel Centre during the war between 1993 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I did not know him. I did, however, mention a person, but I -- I'm sure I was mistaken when I did that. I never had any personal contacts with them. We did not have any business cooperation as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were any of your officers from the engineering administration assigned to the 30th or 40th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody from the engineers administration worked in any of these centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know if someone from the engineering administration served in the Army of Republika Srpska with the assistance of the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN MIHAJLOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how that person left, but there was a colonel, a volunteer. He went there and spent most of the relevant period there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would seek to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My objection is the same, Your Honours. The witness has just spoken about the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres and not about this document. I don't want to interfere with Mr. Saxon's questions, but I think that he should have asked the witness whether he ever heard of this order which is self-explanatory. The witness never said anything about the contents of this document. In order to establish a link between the witness and the document, we should have heard an answer related to the order and not answers related to the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres as we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document discusses the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres, and the witness was able to tell us, explain to us what these centres were and where they were located. So the witness has been able to, in this sense, speak to the contents of the document and, therefore, Your Honour, there is a relationship between this witness and this document. He also identified the signature of General Perisic on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness does know Mr. Perisic. There's no dispute there. In my opinion, the essence of the document is whether members of the Army of Yugoslavia were in breach of rules when they delivered materiel. The witness here as a member of the engineering administration, to talk about the assistance to the Army Republika Srpska, so the contents of the document have nothing to do with the witness. There are references to the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centre, and Mr. Saxon did ask the witness about the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centre. He did not ask him whether he knew anything about this order. This is an order of the Chief of the General Staff sent to somebody. The witness was never asked whether it was ever sent to him. The witness doesn't know anything about this document, Your Honours. If Mr. Saxon wants to insist on this document, I'm going to ask questions in my cross-examination if the Trial Chamber allows me to do so. I believe that Mr. Saxon has not established a link. I don't have anything for this document to be marked for identification. I'm going to draw inference -- I'm going to ask the witness about this document in my cross-examination if you want me to do so, but I believe that based on a term that is mentioned in a document, you cannot ask a witness questions about that and not about the essence of the document, and the essence of the document is an order about materiel and equipment, and my learned friend never asked the witness anything about that. He, rather, asked him about some references in the document about the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is upheld. Anything you want to do with this document, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can it be marked for identification, please, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What did you say about marking for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that it should be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I guess, Madam Registrar, it will be P628 marked for identification under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
